input.title: Card on file at booking
input.body:
Brasserie Lund needs this before their Christmas bookings open on 1 November: a card on file at booking, so a no-show can be charged.

Part of BOK-300 (no-show fees), first release. One fee per restaurant. Online and Google bookings only; a booking a member of staff takes by phone gets no fee. Card storage through PAY-190, which is done.

Acceptance:
- [ ] The guest enters a card on the booking page when the restaurant has fees on.
- [ ] The card is stored through PAY-190 and never in the bookings service.
- [ ] The confirmation says a fee applies and how much.

Source: story round in Qale, 2026-07-17
input.rationale: First of the three stories you kept. The other two need a card on file before they can charge anything.

input.title: Charge the fee after a no-show
input.body:
Brasserie Lund lost about one table a night per restaurant to no-shows last December: this is the charge that makes the card on file worth taking.

Part of BOK-300 (no-show fees), first release. The restaurant decides from the booking list; the charge runs the next morning, so a manager can undo a mistake the same evening. Uses the token PAY-190 stores.

Acceptance:
- [ ] The restaurant marks the booking as a no-show from the booking list.
- [ ] The charge goes through the next morning, not on the spot.
- [ ] The guest gets a receipt by text.

Source: story round in Qale, 2026-07-17
input.rationale: Second of the three stories you kept. Charged the morning after, as the working notes say.

input.title: Fee notice A/B test
input.body:
Brasserie Lund's 40 restaurants get the fee first, so the notice wording gets an A/B test on a few restaurants before every restaurant sees it.

Part of BOK-300 (no-show fees), first release. An A/B test of two wordings of the notice on the booking page, a switch per restaurant, and a report, so we know before December whether the notice costs bookings.

Acceptance:
- [ ] Two wordings of the notice, tested as an A/B test.
- [ ] A restaurant gets one or the other.
- [ ] The report shows completed bookings per wording.

Source: story round in Qale, 2026-07-17
input.rationale: Third of the three stories you kept: the test you said yes to in round one.
